commitMessage: Don't create Link with SWT.WRAP
dslRule:
<!id: swt.link.noWrap>
<!description: Replace SWT.WRAP with SWT.NONE for org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Link constructors to prevent text wrapping.
This aligns with a policy to avoid wrapping for Link widgets, improving display consistency.>
<!severity: WARNING>

new org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Link($parent$, org.eclipse.swt.SWT.WRAP)
=>
new org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Link($parent$, org.eclipse.swt.SWT.NONE)
;;
summary: Replaces the SWT.WRAP style constant with SWT.NONE when creating an org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Link widget, based on an observed project policy.

commitMessage: Use String#replace(..) with chars (more efficient)
dslRule:
<!id: string.replace.single-char-literals>
<!description: Replace String.replace(String, String) with String.replace(char, char) for single-character string literals, for efficiency. This is semantically equivalent as String.replace(CharSequence, CharSequence) treats the CharSequence literally, making it safe to convert to char arguments when applicable.>
<!severity: HINT>
java.lang.String $str.replace($oldS, $newS) :: isStringLiteral($oldS) && $oldS.length() == 1 && isStringLiteral($newS) && $newS.length() == 1
=> $str.replace($oldS.charAt(0), $newS.charAt(0))
;;
summary: Replaces String.replace(String, String) calls with String.replace(char, char) when both arguments are single-character string literals, improving performance without changing semantics.
